text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- New Greens co-leader calls on party to work to topple Kohl
- French central bank president Trichet against franc devaluation
- Strike in confectionery industry spreads
- Retailers disappointed by first shopping Saturday before Christmas
- Gas industry fears EU liberalisation will go too far
- Growing nervousness ahead of EU finance ministers' meeting on stability pact
HANDELSBLATT
- Government's tax reform commission considers compensating cuts in tax breaks with higher value added tax and fuel tax
- Greens elect new co-leader
- Environment Minister Merkel sees possible compromise on disposal of nuclear waste
- Tietmeyer optimistic that single currency will start on schedule
- Deutsche Bank may lose 90 million marks in London fund affair
- Mineral water market stagnates, many producers to be forced out of market
- Row over Daimler-Benz structure continues
- UBS sells Motor-Columbus stake to RWE and Electricite de France
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Greens demand Social Democrats commit themselves to coalition for 1998 election
- Opel not interested in out-of-court settlement with VW
- Stability pact row overshadows meeting of EU finance ministers
- Tietmeter has no objection to stronger dollar
DIE WELT
- Greens demand Social Democrats commit themselves to coalition for 1998 election
- Parliamentary leader of reform communist PDS asks party radicals to moderate line, work for change from within the system
- Retailers disappointed by first shopping Saturday before Christmas
- Unions, health insurers and health professions join in opposition to government health sector reforms
- Opel takes tough line in row with VW
- Strike in confectionery industry spreads
